subject: QBR preflight - infra capacity & unit-econ alignment
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Morales <sara@acme-ml.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR preflight - infra capacity & unit-econ alignment

Team —

Attaching the latest preflight deck and the capacity scenarios CSV for the QBR. Primary ask is to converge on the runway and unit-econ numbers we present to execs on Friday. Key areas I need specific input on by EOD Wednesday (11/4):

- True usable GPU pool (usable v. allocated) for production traffic by model family (llama-70b, rwx-13b). Please list both reserved and burst capacity separately.
- Measured 30/90-day average utilization and p95 latency impact when cache hit is applied (we care about delta on p95 for chat flows).
- Token unit cost delta from our latest quantization rollout + batching settings (examples: 8-bit + batch size 8 v. small-batch low-latency config).
- Any open procurement constraints for converting spot to reserved capacity in EMEA (procurement contact copied).

Quick framing for the QBR narrative: we want to show a 3-line summary — runway (months at 80% nominal demand), top 3 levers (batching, prefix/KV caching, reserved vs spot mix), and a single sensitivity chart that maps p95 latency and $/1000 tokens for three configs.

Attachments: qbr-preflight-deck_v3.pdf, capacity-scenarios.csv

Can each of you reply with the one-slide bullet we should include and any supporting CSVs. I'll stitch into the deck and circulate a runbook for the capacity ask.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Morales <sara@acme-ml.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR preflight - infra capacity & unit-econ alignment

On Mon, Nov 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Attaching the latest preflight deck and the capacity scenarios CSV for the QBR...
> 
> Can each of you reply with the one-slide bullet we should include and any supporting CSVs.

Thanks Irene — quick summary from Product/Capacity side:

- Usable pools today (end of Oct snapshot):
  - llama-70b: reserved 64 GPUs, burst pool (spot+ephemeral) effective 18 GPUs -> usable = 82
  - rwx-13b: reserved 48 GPUs, burst 12 => usable = 60
- 30-day avg utilization (tokens-in-flight normalized): 62% overall; 90-day avg = 58%
- Measured delta when prefix KV cache hits at >= 60%: p95 latency drops ~140ms on llama-70b (median unchanged), tail improves more on rwx-13b (p95 -180ms).
- Batching experiments (attached batching-experiment-summary.csv): switching to continuous batching window=12 reduced effective $/1k tokens by ~9% for non-chat workloads; for chat-heavy workloads gains are 4-6% because cache dominates.

I will own the QBR slide showing utilization, the cache-vs-batch sensitivity, and the recommended default profile (reserve+aggressive cache) for next quarter.

One ask: can Infra confirm procurement runway for converting up to +40 reserved GPUs in EMEA if we need them? If Procurements (copied) can't respond, we'll present a contingency (+20 reserve) and a fallback (increase burst).

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurements Team <procure@bigbank.com>, Sara Morales <sara@acme-ml.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR preflight - infra capacity & unit-econ alignment

Quick operational note / procurement context:

- We can convert spot to reserved in EMEA but lead-time to get committed pricing on next-gen instances is ~3 weeks for the paperwork to lock in. Action: Need SOW + estimated sustained utilization to get finance approval.
- Cost sensitivity: moving 40 GPUs from spot to reserved at our current rate reduces unit $/1k tokens by ~7% but increases fixed monthly commitment by ~$82k. I'll put the modeled P&L in the shared sheet.
- Proposal: for QBR present two scenarios: (A) conservative: +20 reserved (minimal commit), (B) aggressive: +40 reserved (requires exec sign-off & finance).

I'll sync with Procurement offline (procure@bigbank.com) to confirm contract windows and timeline. If any external customers (Sara) need assurances on capacity we should flag which SLAs they require.

-Vivek
Head of Platform Economics
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Morales <sara@acme-ml.com>, Procurements Team <procure@bigbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR preflight - infra capacity & unit-econ alignment

Thanks for the quick turnarounds — helpful and aligned. Final asks before I lock slides tomorrow morning:

1) Lauren: please add the 30/90-day numbers into the capacity-scenarios.csv tab "util-runway" and call out the top-line recommended default config (reserve+cache aggressive) as a single sentence.
2) Vivek: please paste the two scenarios P&L (conservative / aggressive) into qbr-final-inputs.xlsx -> "procurement-scenarios" tab. Highlight the monthly commit delta.
3) Markus / Marissa: any ops caveats (maintenance windows, regional capacity quirks) — send a one-paragraph note; I'll drop under "risks" in the deck.

I've scheduled a 30-minute preflight review with Execs for Thursday 11/5 10:00-10:30 PT (calendar invite sent). Please have the deliverables uploaded to the Drive folder and mark "ready-for-review" in the filename. If we miss EOD Wednesday, we'll default to the conservative scenario in the deck.

Attachments added: qbr-final-inputs.xlsx
Link to folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Infra-Preflight

-Irene
Sr. Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
